Article 10

Parents and/or family in the context of preventing violence against women are responsible for: a. protecting women from conflict and domestic violence that degrades the dignity of women;

b. providing equal opportunities to women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, politics and culture; and

c. preventing violations of women's rights in the household.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms mean:

1. Region is Solok City.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Solok.
4. Regional Apparatus is a supporting element of the Mayor and DPRD in carrying out government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily, develop themselves and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence, and discrimination in the form of preventive, repressive, and post-remedial protection.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
7. Child Rights are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected and fulfilled by parents, family, society, government and the state.
8. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Neglected Child is a child whose needs are not properly met, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social.
10. Street Child is a child whose life is irregular by spending most of their time outside the home to earn a living on the streets or in public places.
11. Regional Child Forum hereinafter referred to as Forda is a forum for child participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and willingness of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
12. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems
13. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing about, during or after the occurrence of violence against the victim.
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Assistance is all actions taken in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social rehabilitation for strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence;
16. Violence is any act that is unlawful with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that creates danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
17. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women, physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
18. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families and the community.
19. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Legal Aid is a legal service provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children.
21. Social Rehabilitation is an effort to reunite victims with their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
22. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.

Article 44

(1) Health services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 42 letter b constitute efforts that include curative and rehabilitative aspects.

(2) Health services for women and children victims of violence are conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.

(3) Special health services for child victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.

(4) Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:

a. medical services; and
b. psychosocial counseling.

Article 56

(1) The Regional Government conducts guidance on the implementation of women and child protection.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out in the form of:

a. conducting socialization of women and child protection programs and activities; and
b. providing training for government officials, law enforcement, religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists, and media managers on prevention and handling of violence against women and children.

Part Six

Social

Article 52

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

(3) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are intended to provide assistance and protection for women and children victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and certainty of their legal rights.

(4) Types of legal assistance services include:

a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of examination minutes;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process in court; d. legal assistance in the court trial process until there is a legally binding decision; and
e. legal assistance in the mediation process.

Article 48

(1) The provision of safe houses as referred to in Article 46 letter b may be provided by the Regional Government.

(2) Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect women and children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

Article 54

(1) Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return women and children victims of violence to their region of origin.

(2) Repatriation of women and children victims of violence is accompanied by social rehabilitation efforts.

(3) The Regional Government carries out repatriation and social rehabilitation of women and children victims of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 19

(1) Regional Governments are obligated to provide comprehensive basic health services for children in the context of fulfilling children's rights in the health sector so that children obtain optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.

(2) Comprehensive basic health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive efforts;
b. preventive efforts;
c. curative efforts; and
d. rehabilitative efforts.
(3) Comprehensive basic health services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be provided free of charge to children with malnutrition, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with human immunodeficiency virus/acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, child laborers, children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, children who are victims of violence, and/or children who are victims of human trafficking.

Article 9

The community in the context of preventing violence against women is responsible for:

a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violence against women; b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and family environment; and
c. preventing unregistered marriages.

Article 47

(1) Counseling services as referred to in Article 46 letter a aim to:

a. assist women and children victims of violence in recognizing their problems and finding effective ways to overcome them independently;
b. provide moral support to women and children victims of violence in facing the process they undergo; c. assist in alleviating, protecting and restoring the physical, psychological, social and spiritual conditions of violence victims so they are able to carry out their social functions normally again; and
d. make victims feel accepted in the community environment.

(2) Counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by gender-responsive social rehabilitation officers, consisting of: a. counselors;

b. psychologists; and
c. psychiatrists.
(3) Counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in a place that guarantees a sense of security, comfort, and confidentiality of information from victims.
(4) The stages of counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. initial counseling;
b. follow-up counseling
c. case discussion (case conference); and
d. location visit (home visit).
(5) Counseling organizers are carried out by:
a. regional apparatus having duties and functions in the social field; b. regional apparatus in charge of women's empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers for women and child empowerment or existing social community organizations; and/or
c. religious institutions.

Article 53

(1) The Regional Government provides legal assistance to women and children victims of violence free of charge.

(2) The Regional Government in providing legal assistance may cooperate with legal aid institutions, advocates and/or other legal assistants.

Article 40

(1) The responsibility of parents and family towards special protection for children is as follows:

a. providing formal and non-formal education in accordance with their talents and interests;
b. caring for, maintaining, educating and protecting children from acts of violence, exploitation, pornography, emergency situations and the possibility of children being in conflict with the law; and
c. facilitating children with special needs and children in conflict with the law as well as children who become victims of violence, exploitation, pornography and emergency situations.
(2) In the event that parents do not exist, or their whereabouts are unknown, or due to a reason cannot carry out their responsibilities, then the responsibility as referred to in paragraph (1) shall transfer to the guardian.

Article 61

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of the City of Solok.

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

(1) Regional Governments are obligated to provide comprehensive basic health services for children in the context of fulfilling children's rights in the health sector so that children obtain optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.

a. promotive efforts;
b. preventive efforts;
c. curative efforts; and

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 56

(1) The Regional Government conducts guidance on the implementation of women and child protection.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out in the form of:

a. conducting socialization of women and child protection programs and activities; and
b. providing training for government officials, law enforcement, religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists, and media managers on prevention and handling of violence against women and children.

Article 57

(1) The Regional Government conducts supervision of the implementation of women and child protection.

(2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out 1 (one) time in 1 (one) year by the Regional Apparatus whose duties and functions are in the field of supervision.

(3) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for women and child protection policies in the Region.

Article 9

The community in the context of preventing violence against women is responsible for:

a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violence against women; b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and family environment; and
c. preventing unregistered marriages.

Article 51

(1) Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 46 letter c is intended for psychological recovery of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principle:

a. not imposing any religion or belief; and b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim.
(3) Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guidance officers, consisting of advisory board consultants, marriage development and preservation bodies 26, religious affairs office officers, Islamic scholars or clerics and/or other religious leaders.

Article 19

(1) Regional Governments are obligated to provide comprehensive basic health services for children in the context of fulfilling children's rights in the health sector so that children obtain optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.

b. preventive efforts;

Article 29

(1) Every person or entity is prohibited from employing and involving children in the worst forms of work.

(2) The worst forms of work as referred to in paragraph (1) are: a. all work in the form of slavery or similar practices; b. all work that exploits, provides or offers children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances or gambling;

c. all work that exploits, provides, or involves children in the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances; and/or

d. all work that endangers the health, safety, or morals of children.

Article 4

Every child has the right:

a. to play, create, participate, grow and develop; b. to freely assemble, associate, live with parents, maintain contact with parents if separated and survival; c. to obtain a name, identity, citizenship, education, child-appropriate information;
d. to obtain health standards in accordance with decent living standards; e. to receive protection and affection from parents; f. to receive protection from exploitation as child labor, minority groups/isolated indigenous groups and from sights or conditions that by their nature are not yet appropriate for children to see; and
g. to receive special protection in critical/emergency situations, displacement/displaced/evicted persons, if experiencing legal conflict and armed conflict or social conflict.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 52

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

(3) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are intended to provide assistance and protection for women and children victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and certainty of their legal rights.

(4) Types of legal assistance services include:

a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of examination minutes;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process in court; d. legal assistance in the court trial process until there is a legally binding decision; and
e. legal assistance in the mediation process.

Article 53

(1) The Regional Government provides legal assistance to women and children victims of violence free of charge.

(2) The Regional Government in providing legal assistance may cooperate with legal aid institutions, advocates and/or other legal assistants.

Article 47

(1) Counseling services as referred to in Article 46 letter a aim to:

a. assist women and children victims of violence in recognizing their problems and finding effective ways to overcome them independently;
b. provide moral support to women and children victims of violence in facing the process they undergo; c. assist in alleviating, protecting and restoring the physical, psychological, social and spiritual conditions of violence victims so they are able to carry out their social functions normally again; and
d. make victims feel accepted in the community environment.

(2) Counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by gender-responsive social rehabilitation officers, consisting of: a. counselors;

b. psychologists; and
c. psychiatrists.
(3) Counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in a place that guarantees a sense of security, comfort, and confidentiality of information from victims.
(4) The stages of counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. initial counseling;
b. follow-up counseling
c. case discussion (case conference); and
d. location visit (home visit).
(5) Counseling organizers are carried out by:
a. regional apparatus having duties and functions in the social field; b. regional apparatus in charge of women's empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers for women and child empowerment or existing social community organizations; and/or
c. religious institutions.

17. 20. Legal Aid is a legal service provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children.
21. Social Rehabilitation is an effort to reunite victims with their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
22. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.

Article 44

(1) Health services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 42 letter b constitute efforts that include curative and rehabilitative aspects.

(2) Health services for women and children victims of violence are conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.

(3) Special health services for child victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.

(4) Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:

a. medical services; and
b. psychosocial counseling.

Article 52

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

(3) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are intended to provide assistance and protection for women and children victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and certainty of their legal rights.

(4) Types of legal assistance services include:

a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of examination minutes;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process in court; d. legal assistance in the court trial process until there is a legally binding decision; and
e. legal assistance in the mediation process.

Article 39

(1) Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return women and children victims of violence to their region of origin.

(3) The Regional Government carries out repatriation and social rehabilitation of women and children victims of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

(1) The Regional Government in order to administer women's empowerment and child protection affairs may establish UPTD PPA.

(2) UPTD PPA functions to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.

a. provide services and handling as soon as possible to women and children experiencing problems;

Social rehabilitation services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 42 letter c are aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of victims who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

(1) Health services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 42 letter b constitute efforts that include curative and rehabilitative aspects.

(2) Health services for women and children victims of violence are conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.

(3) Special health services for child victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.

(4) Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:

a. medical services; and
b. psychosocial counseling.

Article 47

(1) Counseling services as referred to in Article 46 letter a aim to:

a. assist women and children victims of violence in recognizing their problems and finding effective ways to overcome them independently;
b. provide moral support to women and children victims of violence in facing the process they undergo; c. assist in alleviating, protecting and restoring the physical, psychological, social and spiritual conditions of violence victims so they are able to carry out their social functions normally again; and
d. make victims feel accepted in the community environment.

(2) Counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by gender-responsive social rehabilitation officers, consisting of: a. counselors;

b. psychologists; and
c. psychiatrists.
(3) Counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in a place that guarantees a sense of security, comfort, and confidentiality of information from victims.
(4) The stages of counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. initial counseling;
b. follow-up counseling
c. case discussion (case conference); and
d. location visit (home visit).
(5) Counseling organizers are carried out by:
a. regional apparatus having duties and functions in the social field; b. regional apparatus in charge of women's empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers for women and child empowerment or existing social community organizations; and/or
c. religious institutions.

Article 19

(1) Regional Governments are obligated to provide comprehensive basic health services for children in the context of fulfilling children's rights in the health sector so that children obtain optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.

(2) Comprehensive basic health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive efforts;
b. preventive efforts;
c. curative efforts; and
d. rehabilitative efforts.
(3) Comprehensive basic health services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be provided free of charge to children with malnutrition, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with human immunodeficiency virus/acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, child laborers, children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, children who are victims of violence, and/or children who are victims of human trafficking.

Article 55

(1) The Regional Government in order to administer women's empowerment and child protection affairs may establish UPTD PPA.

(2) UPTD PPA functions to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.

(3) The scope of UPTD PPA services includes complaint services, consultation, mediation, outreach, health, social rehabilitation, spiritual guidance, assistance, law enforcement and legal assistance, and repatriation and social rehabilitation services.

(4) In carrying out its functions as referred to in paragraph (2) UPTD PPA is obliged to:

a. provide services and handling as soon as possible to women and children experiencing problems;
b. provide ease, comfort, safety and free of charge to women and children experiencing problems; c. maintain confidentiality of women and children experiencing problems;and
d. guarantee justice and legal certainty for women and children experiencing problems.
(5) Further provisions regarding the organization and working procedures of UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 52

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

(3) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are intended to provide assistance and protection for women and children victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and certainty of their legal rights.

(4) Types of legal assistance services include:

a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of examination minutes;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process in court; d. legal assistance in the court trial process until there is a legally binding decision; and
e. legal assistance in the mediation process.

Article 53

(1) The Regional Government provides legal assistance to women and children victims of violence free of charge.

(2) The Regional Government in providing legal assistance may cooperate with legal aid institutions, advocates and/or other legal assistants.

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

Article 47

(1) Counseling services as referred to in Article 46 letter a aim to:

a. assist women and children victims of violence in recognizing their problems and finding effective ways to overcome them independently;
b. provide moral support to women and children victims of violence in facing the process they undergo; c. assist in alleviating, protecting and restoring the physical, psychological, social and spiritual conditions of violence victims so they are able to carry out their social functions normally again; and
d. make victims feel accepted in the community environment.

(2) Counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by gender-responsive social rehabilitation officers, consisting of: a. counselors;

b. psychologists; and
c. psychiatrists.

a. initial counseling;
b. follow-up counseling
c. case discussion (case conference); and
d. location visit (home visit).

a. regional apparatus having duties and functions in the social field; b. regional apparatus in charge of women's empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers for women and child empowerment or existing social community organizations; and/or
c. religious institutions.

Article 52

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 25

Every child who is in an educational unit environment shall be protected from acts of violence.

Article 44

(1) Health services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 42 letter b constitute efforts that include curative and rehabilitative aspects.

(2) Health services for women and children victims of violence are conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, quality and conducted in accordance with health service standards.

(3) Special health services for child victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.

(4) Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:

a. medical services; and
b. psychosocial counseling.

Article 52

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

(3) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are intended to provide assistance and protection for women and children victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and certainty of their legal rights.

(4) Types of legal assistance services include:

a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of examination minutes;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process in court; d. legal assistance in the court trial process until there is a legally binding decision; and
e. legal assistance in the mediation process.

Article 45

Social rehabilitation services for women and children victims of violence as referred to in Article 42 letter c are aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of victims who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

Article 47

(1) Counseling services as referred to in Article 46 letter a aim to:

a. assist women and children victims of violence in recognizing their problems and finding effective ways to overcome them independently;
b. provide moral support to women and children victims of violence in facing the process they undergo; c. assist in alleviating, protecting and restoring the physical, psychological, social and spiritual conditions of violence victims so they are able to carry out their social functions normally again; and
d. make victims feel accepted in the community environment.

(2) Counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by gender-responsive social rehabilitation officers, consisting of: a. counselors;

b. psychologists; and
c. psychiatrists.
(3) Counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in a place that guarantees a sense of security, comfort, and confidentiality of information from victims.
(4) The stages of counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. initial counseling;
b. follow-up counseling
c. case discussion (case conference); and
d. location visit (home visit).
(5) Counseling organizers are carried out by:
a. regional apparatus having duties and functions in the social field; b. regional apparatus in charge of women's empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers for women and child empowerment or existing social community organizations; and/or
c. religious institutions.

Article 48

(1) The provision of safe houses as referred to in Article 46 letter b may be provided by the Regional Government.

(2) Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect women and children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

Article 9

a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may lead to violence against women; b. strengthening the role of community organizations, religious organizations and family environment; and
c. preventing unregistered marriages.

(1) Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 46 letter c is intended for psychological recovery of women and children victims of violence.

(2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principle:

a. not imposing any religion or belief; and b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim.
(3) Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guidance officers, consisting of advisory board consultants, marriage development and preservation bodies 26, religious affairs office officers, Islamic scholars or clerics and/or other religious leaders.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

(3) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for women and child protection policies in the Region.

IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

(3) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are intended to provide assistance and protection for women and children victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and certainty of their legal rights.

(4) Types of legal assistance services include:

a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of examination minutes;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process in court; d. legal assistance in the court trial process until there is a legally binding decision; and
e. legal assistance in the mediation process.

Article 39

(1) The community, ninik mamak, alim ulama, cadiak pandai, bundo kanduang in the context of special protection for children are responsible for:

a. providing support for the development of special protection programs for children;
b. playing an active role in responding to symptoms that occur in the community that potentially violate children's rights;
c. conducting monitoring and supervision of the implementation of special protection for children; and
d. providing information and or reporting if violence against children occurs to the integrated service center for women and children empowerment or the authorities.
(2) The responsibility of the community, ninik mamak, alim ulama, cadiak pandai, bundo kanduang as referred to in paragraph (1) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 47

(1) Counseling services as referred to in Article 46 letter a aim to:

a. assist women and children victims of violence in recognizing their problems and finding effective ways to overcome them independently;
b. provide moral support to women and children victims of violence in facing the process they undergo; c. assist in alleviating, protecting and restoring the physical, psychological, social and spiritual conditions of violence victims so they are able to carry out their social functions normally again; and

(2) Counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by gender-responsive social rehabilitation officers, consisting of: a. counselors;

b. psychologists; and
c. psychiatrists.

a. initial counseling;
b. follow-up counseling
c. case discussion (case conference); and

a. regional apparatus having duties and functions in the social field; b. regional apparatus in charge of women's empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers for women and child empowerment or existing social community organizations; and/or

Article 5

(1) The Regional Government is responsible for organizing the protection of women by involving the active role of parents, families, ninik mamak, cadiak pandai, alim ulama, bundo kanduang, customary leaders, religious leaders, the community, and institutions in the field of women's protection.

(2) The responsibility of the Regional Government in organizing the protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by regional apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 4

Every child has the right:

a. to play, create, participate, grow and develop; b. to freely assemble, associate, live with parents, maintain contact with parents if separated and survival; c. to obtain a name, identity, citizenship, education, child-appropriate information;

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of regional government is to make regional policies with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. This shows that female Children should be protected by the state, especially from Violence because their Rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and Violence against women and Children, especially for the City of Solok region. The City of Solok is one of the parties most authorized to carry out women's empowerment and Child Protection by conducting and formulating regulations to provide guarantees for the implementation of Women and Children Protection.

One form of such regulation is the Regional Regulation of the City of Solok. This regulation is expected to be able to encourage efforts to improve the physical and mental condition of women and Children victims of Violence.

I. GENERAL

The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and administer its own region for the realization of public welfare through improved Service, empowerment and community participation. In addition, the 1945 Constitution has also mandated in Article 28D paragraph (1) that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, Protection and just legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph 2 also states that every Child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to Protection from Violence and discrimination. II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 55

(1) The Regional Government in order to administer women's empowerment and child protection affairs may establish UPTD PPA.

(2) UPTD PPA functions to provide services to women and children experiencing criminal and civil problems.

(3) The scope of UPTD PPA services includes complaint services, consultation, mediation, outreach, health, social rehabilitation, spiritual guidance, assistance, law enforcement and legal assistance, and repatriation and social rehabilitation services.

(4) In carrying out its functions as referred to in paragraph (2) UPTD PPA is obliged to:

a. provide services and handling as soon as possible to women and children experiencing problems;
b. provide ease, comfort, safety and free of charge to women and children experiencing problems; c. maintain confidentiality of women and children experiencing problems;and
d. guarantee justice and legal certainty for women and children experiencing problems.
(5) Further provisions regarding the organization and working procedures of UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 36

(1) The Regional Government facilitates the establishment of Forda in implementing the fulfillment of children's rights to express opinions and participate.

(2) Forda as referred to in paragraph (1) represents children, both representation of children's geographical domicile, components of children's socio-cultural groups and children's educational background.

(3) In every formulation of policies related to children, the Regional Government must pay attention to and accommodate children's opinions submitted through Forda.

(4) Further provisions regarding the establishment of Forda as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2) and paragraph (3) shall be stipulated by Mayor's Decree.

Article 52

(1) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women and children, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

(3) Law enforcement and legal assistance services are intended to provide assistance and protection for women and children victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and certainty of their legal rights.

(4) Types of legal assistance services include:

a. legal assistance in the reporting process and preparation of examination minutes;
b. legal assistance in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal assistance in the examination process in court; d. legal assistance in the court trial process until there is a legally binding decision; and
e. legal assistance in the mediation process.

Article 19

(1) Regional Governments are obligated to provide comprehensive basic health services for children in the context of fulfilling children's rights in the health sector so that children obtain optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.

(2) Comprehensive basic health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotive efforts;
b. preventive efforts;
c. curative efforts; and
d. rehabilitative efforts.
(3) Comprehensive basic health services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be provided free of charge to children with malnutrition, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with human immunodeficiency virus/acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, child laborers, children who are victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, children who are victims of violence, and/or children who are victims of human trafficking.

Part Four

Article 47

(1) Counseling services as referred to in Article 46 letter a aim to:

a. assist women and children victims of violence in recognizing their problems and finding effective ways to overcome them independently;
b. provide moral support to women and children victims of violence in facing the process they undergo; c. assist in alleviating, protecting and restoring the physical, psychological, social and spiritual conditions of violence victims so they are able to carry out their social functions normally again; and
d. make victims feel accepted in the community environment.

(2) Counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by gender-responsive social rehabilitation officers, consisting of: a. counselors;

b. psychologists; and
c. psychiatrists.
(3) Counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in a place that guarantees a sense of security, comfort, and confidentiality of information from victims.
(4) The stages of counseling services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. initial counseling;
b. follow-up counseling
c. case discussion (case conference); and
d. location visit (home visit).
(5) Counseling organizers are carried out by:
a. regional apparatus having duties and functions in the social field; b. regional apparatus in charge of women's empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers for women and child empowerment or existing social community organizations; and/or
c. religious institutions.
